name: Roast Beef with Yorkshire Pudding
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: eggs, whites and yolks beaten separately
ingredients.originalText: 4 eggs, whites and yolks beaten separately

instructions.text: Set a piece of beef to roast upon a grating, or several sticks laid across a dripping-pan
Three-quarters of an hour before it is done, mix the pudding and pour into the pan
Continue to roast the beef, the dripping meanwhile falling upon the latter below
For the pudding: mix together 1 pint of milk, 4 eggs with whites and yolks beaten separately, 2 cups of prepared flour, and 1 teaspoonful salt
Be careful, in mixing, not to get the batter too stiff
If there is much fat in the dripping-pan before the pudding is ready to be put in, drain it off, leaving just enough to prevent the batter from sticking to the bottom
When both are done, cut the pudding into squares, and lay around the meat when dished

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Set a piece of beef to roast upon a grating, or several sticks laid across a dripping-pan
2. Three-quarters of an hour before it is done, mix the pudding and pour into the pan
3. Continue to roast the beef, the dripping meanwhile falling upon the latter below
4. For the pudding: mix together 1 pint of milk, 4 eggs with whites and yolks beaten separately, 2 cups of prepared flour, and 1 teaspoonful salt
5. Be careful, in mixing, not to get the batter too stiff
6. If there is much fat in the dripping-pan before the pudding is ready to be put in, drain it off, leaving just enough to prevent the batter from sticking to the bottom
7. When both are done, cut the pudding into squares, and lay around the meat when dished
